claims: The Artemis II crew returned to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The splashdown concluded a 10-day journey around the Moon.
The Artemis II crew had recovery by the USS John P. Murtha.
The capsule hit the upper atmosphere at roughly 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Drogue parachutes deployed around 8:03 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Main parachutes deployed at 8:04 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
Splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II astronauts were extracted and transferred via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha by 9:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission concluded after 10 days.
The Artemis II mission tested the Orion spacecraft with a crew on board for the first time.
